what_its_for: This combination medicine helps control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works in two ways: ertugliflozin helps your kidneys remove extra sugar from your body through your urine, and metformin helps your liver make less sugar and helps your body use insulin better. It is used along with diet and exercise to manage type 2 diabetes.
how_to_take: Take this tablet by mouth twice a day with food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Taking it with food helps reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Drink plenty of water throughout the day while taking this medicine. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully and do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you based on your current diabetes medicines, your kidney function, and how well your blood sugar is controlled. Common doses range from 2.5 mg/500 mg to 7.5 mg/1000 mg per tablet, taken twice daily. Never take more than the amount your doctor prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose as usual. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase the risk of a serious condition called lactic acidosis and can also affect your blood sugar levels. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough fluids daily, especially during hot weather, exercise, or when you are sick. Do not take this medicine if you need to have imaging tests with iodine-based contrast dye (such as a CT scan) without first talking to your doctor, as you may need to temporarily stop taking it. Avoid sitting in extreme heat for long periods and tell any doctor or dentist that you take this medicine before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, stomach pain, nausea or vomiting, feeling cold, dizzy, or lightheaded (these could be signs of lactic acidosis, a rare but serious side effect); signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning when you urinate, frequent urination, or cloudy urine with fever; signs of a genital yeast infection such as itching, burning, or unusual discharge; signs of a serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene including pain, tenderness, redness, or swelling in the genital or rectal area with fever; signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, confusion, or fast heartbeat; signs of ketoacidosis such as nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, or trouble breathing even if your blood sugar seems normal; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Metformin begins working within a few days, but it may take 2 to 4 weeks to see a noticeable improvement in your blood sugar levels. Ertugliflozin can start reducing blood sugar within a few days as well. However, the full benefit of this combination medicine is usually seen after several weeks of consistent use along with healthy eating and regular exercise. Keep taking your medicine every day even if you feel well, because type 2 diabetes often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Kidney problems: This medicine is not recommended if your kidneys are not working well. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. Do not take this medicine if your estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is below 45 mL/min/1.73 m². Liver problems: This medicine is not recommended for people with liver disease. Older adults: If you are 65 or older, your doctor will monitor you more closely because older adults may be at higher risk for kidney problems and dehydration. Pregnancy: This medicine is not recommended during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is approved for use in adults only.
